intuition: Collect the tree's levels from the root downward using a queue. Then reverse the list of levels. Reverse only the groups, keeping values within each group in left-to-right order. This gives the required bottom-up result with a simple, consistent traversal.

At the start of a breadth-first round, the queue contains exactly the nodes for one depth. Save its length before processing them. The children appended during this round belong to the next depth and must wait until the next round. Enqueue each left child before its right child to preserve the required spatial ordering.

The distinction between reversing the outer list and reversing each row matters. The task wants deepest levels first but still left-to-right values inside every level. A final outer slice reversal changes only depth order. Queue size is bounded by tree width, and the complete answer necessarily stores every node value.
An empty root yields no levels, while a singleton produces one one-element group.

steps: For [3,9,20,null,null,15,7], the initial queue contains only root 3.

Freeze level_size=2. Process 9 and 20, saving [9,20] and enqueueing 15 then 7.
Process the final queue to save [15,7]. No more children remain.
Reverse only the groups to return [[15,7],[9,20],[3]].
